definition: Artificial Intelligence System (AIS) was a volunteer computing project undertaken by Intelligence Realm, Inc.
details: with the long-term goal of simulating the human brain in real time, complete with artificial consciousness and artificial general intelligence. They claimed to have found, in research, the "mechanisms of knowledge representation in the brain which is equivalent to finding artificial intelligence", before moving into the developmental phase.

explainer.lead: Artificial Intelligence System (AIS) was a volunteer-computing project run by Intelligence Realm, Inc. It aimed to simulate the human brain in real time and ultimately achieve artificial consciousness and artificial general intelligence, making it an ambitious example of distributed computing applied to brain-inspired AI research.

tiers.eli5: Imagine many people lending their computers’ spare time to one huge science project, like neighbors combining small puzzle-solving efforts. AIS wanted to use that shared effort to work toward a computer simulation of the human brain. Its ultimate hopes were a machine that could think generally and be conscious, but those were goals rather than demonstrated achievements.
tiers.practitioner: AIS belongs to the volunteer-computing setting: participants contribute computer time to a shared research project rather than running everything on one organization’s machines. Its proposed application was brain simulation, informed by claimed research into mechanisms of knowledge representation. No software stack, model architecture, workload format, or performance results are specified, so it should not be treated as a ready-made engineering framework.
tiers.paperLevel: AIS is defined as a volunteer-computing project by Intelligence Realm, Inc., with the objective of real-time human-brain simulation incorporating artificial consciousness and artificial general intelligence. The project claimed that its research had identified mechanisms of knowledge representation in the brain and equated that finding with finding artificial intelligence before entering development. No formal algorithm, architecture, benchmark, or evidence of achieving the stated goals is provided.

explainer.example: A volunteer could offer spare computer time to AIS instead of leaving that capacity unused. That contribution would join the project’s wider computing effort, whose intended research path led from knowledge-representation mechanisms toward a real-time human-brain simulation.

explainer.intuition: The idea was to combine volunteers’ computing resources in pursuit of a problem too ambitious for a small, isolated effort: simulating the human brain. AIS connected that distributed-computing approach with research claims about how knowledge is represented in the brain.
howItWorks: Volunteers contribute computing resources to the AIS project.
The shared effort supports research into knowledge representation in the brain.
The project reports finding relevant mechanisms and moves into a developmental phase.
Development is directed toward real-time brain simulation, with artificial consciousness and general intelligence as long-term goals.
explainer.whyItMatters: AIS illustrates how volunteer computing can be applied to highly ambitious AI and brain-simulation goals. It also shows the importance of distinguishing a project’s research claims and long-term aspirations from demonstrated technical capabilities.
misconceptions: AIS was not described as a completed real-time simulation of the human brain.
Artificial consciousness and artificial general intelligence were long-term goals, not established results.
The claim about discovering knowledge-representation mechanisms does not by itself specify or validate a working general-intelligence system.
